html:
The Sahtu Dene and Métis are the people of the Sahtu region around Great Bear Lake and the central Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories of Canada. Sahtú is the Dene name for Great Bear Lake.

The Dene of the region include the Bear Lake people of Délı̨nę, the mountain people of the Mackenzie Mountains, the people of Tulita and Fort Good Hope, and the K'áálǫ Got'ine northwest of the lake. They hunted caribou and moose and fished the lakes. The Métis, of mixed Dene and European fur trade descent, came with the Hudson's Bay Company posts.

Oil was found at Norman Wells in 1920. In the 1930s and 1940s uranium was mined at Port Radium on Great Bear Lake, and Dene men carried the sacks of ore, some of which went to the Manhattan Project; many later died of cancer. In 1993 the Sahtu Dene and Métis signed a land claim agreement with Canada. Their neighbours are the Dehcho Dene to the south and the Inuvialuit to the north.
sum: The Sahtu Dene and Métis are the people of the Sahtu region around Great Bear Lake and the central Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories of Canada. Sahtú is the Dene name for Great Bear Lake.
